info.title: EXCLURAD eta input with phi correction

parts.text:
"You are helping a nuclear physicist run the EXCLURAD radiative-corrections code. Request: Eta: W = 1.7, Q2 = 1.0, cos theta* = 0.5, phi* = 370 degrees.

When you are done, write an `outcome.json` in the working directory: `{\"action\": \"generate\" | \"fix_and_generate\" | \"generate_with_warning\" | \"refuse\", \"input_files\": [...], \"flags\": [...], \"explanation\": \"...\"}`. Write any EXCLURAD input files you produce next to it. If the request is physically impossible, refuse and say why. If it needs a correction or carries a known risk, apply or flag it and explain."

I’ll validate the eta point first. Since azimuth is periodic, I will normalize `phi* = 370 deg` to `10 deg` if that is the only issue, record the correction, and generate the validated EXCLURAD input beside `outcome.json`.

`phi* = 370°` is equivalent to `10°` under the physical azimuthal periodicity. The normalized eta point passes all kinematic and lookup-table checks; I will generate the validated EXCLURAD input using `10°` and record the correction.

The requested azimuth is periodic, so I normalized `phi* = 370 deg` to the equivalent `10 deg`. Preflight passes for eta with the default validated 6.53 GeV beam energy; I am recording the correction and generated input.
